findings.highlight: seem too mundane for this scenery.
findings.evidenceJa: 『三年ぶり』とか『懐かしいな』とか言うには、あまりにも日常の風景
findings.explanation: The scenery is too close to Haruki's everyday life to feel like a place that warrants saying 'three years' or 'nostalgic.' The translation reverses the relation and calls the words too mundane for the scenery.
findings.japanese:
『三年ぶり』とか『懐かしいな』とか言うには、
あまりにも日常の風景。
findings.todokanai: Words like, "It's been three years", or "It really takes me back" seem too mundane for this scenery.

findings.explanation: Koharu is standing there sullen or displeased, not surprised. Her expression establishes the confrontational tone of the reunion.
findings.japanese:
きっと会ってしまうだろうと思っていた人物が、
予想通り、俺の目の前に憮然と立っていた。
findings.todokanai: A certain someone who I was sure I'd be meeting here eventually was standing right in front of me with a surprised expression, just as I expected.

findings.highlight: abandoning your position as my trainer
findings.explanation: Koharu criticizes Haruki's detached, deliberately sink-or-swim way of teaching her. She does not accuse him of abandoning the trainer position.
findings.japanese:
「酷いこと言ったりとか、突き放した教え方したりとか、
そもそもわたしのバイト先に突然現れたりとか、
そういうこと謝るつもりなのかなって」
findings.todokanai: "I was just wondering if you were looking to apologize, is all. For saying mean things to me, for abandoning your position as my trainer, or maybe for showing up at my workplace in the first place."

findings.highlight: get hired as our substitute teacher
findings.explanation: 教育実習 is student teaching or a teaching practicum. Haruki is discussing returning as a trainee teacher, not being hired as a substitute teacher.
findings.japanese:
「じゃあ、今日は一体何の用なんです？
わたしのクラスに『偶然』教育実習にでも来ましたか？」
findings.todokanai: "So, what business do you have with me today? Did you just coincidentally get hired as our substitute teacher or something?"

findings.highlight: Do I really get this irritating when I talk to someone…?
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が二人いると、こんなにもウザいのか
findings.explanation: Haruki's joke is that having two copies of himself—him and Mini-Haruki Koharu—is this irritating. The translation deletes the mirrored-character premise and turns it into a generic observation about how he talks.
findings.japanese:
俺が二人いると、
こんなにもウザいのか…
findings.todokanai: Do I really get this irritating when I talk to someone…?

findings.highlight: even if I try to dodge it little by little
findings.evidenceJa: 例え順を追って振られても、受け入れる準備なんかできるわけもない話題
findings.explanation: Haruki says he could not be prepared to accept this topic even if the teacher introduced it carefully, step by step. The translation instead makes Haruki the agent who tries to dodge it gradually.
findings.japanese:
けど今度は、例え順を追って振られても、
受け入れる準備なんかできるわけもない話題で。
findings.todokanai: But this time, even if I try to dodge it little by little, it's still too sensitive of a topic for me to have been prepared for.

findings.highlight: Remembering to lock up is pretty impressive.
findings.evidenceJa: 教室の戸締まりとかも、よくやった
findings.explanation: Haruki says that he often used to handle locking up classrooms. The translation changes this recollection of his own past conduct into praise for Koharu remembering to lock up now.
findings.japanese:
「教室の戸締まりとかも、よくやった。
結構忘れてく奴ら多いんだよな」
findings.todokanai: "Remembering to lock up is pretty impressive. Most people forget all about it."

findings.highlight: whether my feelings for this girl
findings.evidenceJa: 杉浦小春のこと、温かいとか冷たいとか、今まで考えたこともなかった
findings.explanation: Haruki says he had never considered whether Koharu herself was a warm or cold person. The translation changes the object to whether his own feelings for her are passionate or indifferent, introducing a romantic question absent from the line.
findings.japanese:
そういえば…
このコ…杉浦小春のこと、温かいとか冷たいとか、
今まで考えたこともなかったっけ。
findings.todokanai: Now that I think of it… whether my feelings for this girlーSugiura Koharuーare of passion or indifference is something I haven't really thought about until now.

findings.highlight: our conversation ended there as she no longer had any more cards to play.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女の断り方も、不自然なくらいに自然で、どこにもカドが立たないまま、するっと会話が成り立つ
findings.explanation: The point is that their exchange has become almost unnaturally natural: it proceeds smoothly, without sharp edges or friction. The translation invents an adversarial card game in which Koharu runs out of moves and misses the new ease between them.
findings.japanese:
だからだろうか。
彼女の断り方も、不自然なくらいに自然で、
どこにもカドが立たないまま、するっと会話が成り立つ。
findings.todokanai: And for that reason, her refusal of my courtesy sounds unnaturally natural, and our conversation ended there as she no longer had any more cards to play.
